id: Insect Molecular Biology - 2001 - Ranson - Identification of a point mutation in the voltage‐gated sodium channel gene of

is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae (Title: 'Identification of a point mutation in the voltage-gated sodium channel gene of Kenyan Anopheles gambiae').

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports the discovery and genotyping of the leucine-serine mutation at position 1014 (Vgsc L1014S, which corresponds to Vgsc L995S) (Abstract, Page 4).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Genotype data for a 1999 field collection is provided on page 4: 'In 1999 a further forty-two An. gambiae s.l. were collected... identified three individuals that were heterozygous for the kdr mutation... All the remaining individuals were homozygous for the wild-type susceptible allele.' (3 RS, 39 SS, N=42).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from villages approximately 50 km north-west of Kisumu, Kenya, in 1986, 1992, and 1999 (Page 4).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study describing the identification of a new kdr mutation and its frequency in field populations.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is tied to villages approximately 50 km north-west of Kisumu, Kenya (Page 4).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The field collection data is specifically attributed to the year 1999 (Page 4).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The paper describes the original identification of the L1014S mutation in Kenya and reports a specific 1999 field collection; there is no indication this data is a subset of a larger published dataset.

supplement.evidence: All relevant genotype counts for the field population and linkage analysis are contained within the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: The study identifies the Vgsc L1014S (L995S) mutation, also known as kdr-east, in Anopheles gambiae from Western Kenya. It provides genotype frequencies for a field collection of 42 mosquitoes from 1999 (3 RS, 39 SS) and demonstrates a significant correlation between the mutation and permethrin resistance through linkage analysis of F2 progeny from genetic crosses (Table 2).
